title: Platform Seller QuickSwap Battlepack (draft)
content:
Purpose: a compact, skimmable battlepack for platform sellers to run a 10–15 minute technical qualification + rapid demo, and to execute QuickSwap fallback moves when customers raise cost/latency concerns. This is intentionally minimal: one page per persona, micro-scripts, and two fallback paths (economics-first, reliability-first).

Audience: platform sellers, SEs, SDRs with technical affinity. Not a full playbook — use in tandem with canary/fallback playbook (linked).

How to use: keep this on Slack as a single file during live calls. Use the "swap" lines verbatim when steering customers between hosted/dedicated/private options.

Topline positioning (30s):
- Redwood = predictable inference economics + production-grade SLAs.
- We unify one API + routing layer across Hosted, Dedicated, Private — same integration, different guarantees.
- Practical opener: "Most teams pick a hosted API to ship. We help you keep that speed while giving you a predictable path to reserve capacity or VPC when you need tighter latency/cost control."

Quick metrics cheat (for verbal use):
- Typical p95 generation latency (hosted, mid-size model, 512 tokens): ~120–220ms depending on region/config.
- Embedding pipeline: bulk 10k docs can be batched to reduce per-doc cost by ~3–5x vs naive calls.
- Cost examples: hosted: $X per 1k tokens (use pricing page); dedicated: ~40–70% lower unit cost at sustained throughput with reserved commits. (Do not quote exact $ without checking pricing page)

Persona cards (one-line problem → one-line solution → swap lines):
1) Platform Architect / Infra Lead
- Problem: needs predictable throughput for peak traffic, worried about multi-tenant noisy neighbors and burst spikes.
- Solution: Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling + regional routing; optional private control plane for network isolation.
- Swap line (if probing cost): "If reserved commit looks heavy, we can start with a burst-enabled Dedicated pool for predictable bursts and then move to full commit after an initial month of usage telemetry."
- Swap line (if probing privacy): "We can ship the same API to you on a Private deployment — identical developer experience, different networking and key management."

2) Product Manager / PM leading an ML feature
- Problem: cares about iteration speed, low friction for product teams, and avoiding regressions after model upgrades.
- Solution: Hosted API to prototype + Redwood Optimize for quantization/batching suggestions and integrated evals to catch regressions.
- Swap line: "Ship on hosted for two sprints; when you see stable quality and load, we’ll run a dedicated economics pass and show a direct forecast for cost-per-endpoint."

3) CTO / Head of Reliability
- Problem: needs SLAs, runbooks, and graceful fallbacks during incidents.
- Solution: Redwood Console provides per-route SLOs, canary rollouts, automatic fallbacks to cheaper model variants, and tracing hooks for observability.
- Swap line: "We can demo the canary rollback in 10 minutes — show you step-throughs of an A/B rollout and how automatic fallback triggers on latency or error spikes."

Micro-scripts: short responses to common objections (use conversational tone)
- Objection: "We can host models ourselves cheaper."
  Response: "Totally — but what we see repeatedly is that small infra differences (batching, kernel selection, KV cache) cause 20–60% variance in unit cost. Redwood reduces that variance and gives you predictable economics without locking you into a single infra layer."
- Objection: "We need on-prem for data residency."
  Response: "We offer Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) with the same API and rollout tooling. Many customers prototype on hosted, then flip to Private for regulated workloads with minimal dev changes."
- Objection: "Latency spikes worry me."
  Response: "We layer caching, continuous batching, and fallback to compatible model variants. If you want, we can show a recorded incident replay and the automated fallback timeline in the Console."

QuickSwap fallback flows (two condensed playbooks):
1) Economics-first QuickSwap (when cost concerns dominate)
- Step 1: Ask for 3–5 sample requests / token distribution (or share usage dashboard link).
- Step 2: Propose a short dedicated pilot: 2–4 week reserved capacity with burst buffer. Present forecast: compare current hosted spend vs pilot (show 3 scenarios: low/expected/high usage).
- Step 3: Offer auto rollback to hosted if forecasted unit cost isn’t met after pilot.
- Key line: "This gives you a measurable view of unit economics in production without long-term lock-in."

2) Reliability-first QuickSwap (when latency/SLA dominate)
- Step 1: Map critical routes and SLO targets (p50/p95/p99).
- Step 2: Run a mini-canary on Dedicated with canary policy to test real traffic shape.
- Step 3: Configure fallthrough routing (preferred region → fallback region → cheaper model variant) and demo failover in a scheduled maintenance window.
- Key line: "Same API, but we add an isolation layer and deterministic routing rules so critical traffic bypasses noisy tenants."

Demo checklist (10–12 minutes):
- 0:00–1:00: Quick problem recap and persona check.
- 1:00–3:00: Show integration (API call, streaming or batch) — emphasize same SDK experience across modes.
- 3:00–6:00: Switch to Console: show per-route latency and cost for last 24h, demonstrate a canary rollout toggle.
- 6:00–8:00: Trigger simulated spike and show automatic fallback to model variant.
- 8:00–10:00: Discuss cost forecast and propose QuickSwap pilot. Leave 2 minutes for next steps and follow-up items.

Evidence snippets (one-liners to cite quickly):
- "Several mid-market SaaS customers reduced per-token spend by ~35% after moving stable workloads to Dedicated with our batching/quantization recommendations."
- "Our routing policies keep user-facing routes on higher-tier capacity and route non-critical jobs to lower-cost pools automatically."

Callouts to include in slides/emails:
- Include a single pane screenshot of Console per-route view (redacted) and a small graph showing canary rollback event.
- Attach or link a short CSV sample (5k rows) for embedding cost forecast exercise.

Open questions (for product/solutions follow-up):
- Do we want a templated cost forecast spreadsheet per common vertical (marketplace, support, search) to standardize proposals?
- Can SEs get a single CLI to spin up a 2-week dedicated pilot with prefilled defaults? (Action: solutions eng to prototype)

Next steps / owner:
- Maya to circulate v0.1 to SEs and run 2 seller rehearsals this week.
- Diego to prepare a mini-demo dataset and Console link for rehearsals (target: 2026-02-12).
- Priya to draft a one-pager for legal/finance on pilot terms and rollback SLAs.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep language non-committal on exact $ unless pricing page is referenced.
- Add more vertical examples in next iteration (adtech, legal, healthcare).
- Consider a "swap card" UI in Console that shows recommended mode for a route based on cost/latency vs SLOs.

Links referenced in-conversation: Confluence quickswap draft, JIRA G2M-812, demo scripts PR (link above).

End of doc — this is intentionally compact. Use it during calls and report back friction points in the quick feedback thread (Slack #g2m-quickswap).
